so I would like to build and events page to the website and create a new Google sheet where all the form details would go to, each event sectioned by new sheet tabs.  10. GOOGLE SHEETS INTEGRATION – CENTRAL EVENT REGISTRATION DATABASE

This is a critical requirement.

I want all event registrations across The AffluentAccelerators website to be automatically collected and organised inside ONE central Google Sheets document.

Do not create a separate Google Spreadsheet for every event.

Instead, create one master spreadsheet with multiple worksheets (tabs), where each event has its own dedicated tab.

A. MASTER GOOGLE SPREADSHEET

Create or connect to a Google Spreadsheet named:

THE AFFLUENTACCELERATORS – EVENTS & REGISTRATION DATABASE

The spreadsheet should contain the following structure:

1. OVERVIEW DASHBOARD
2. ALL REGISTRATIONS
3. EVENT 001 – ONLINE BUSINESS MEETUP & SPOTLIGHT
4. EVENT 002 – [NEXT EVENT NAME]
5. EVENT 003 – [NEXT EVENT NAME]

Additional event tabs should be created automatically as new events are configured.

B. AUTOMATIC EVENT TAB CREATION

Whenever an administrator creates and publishes a new event, the system should:

1. Check whether the event already has an assigned Google Sheets worksheet.
2. If one exists, reuse it.
3. If one does not exist, automatically create a new worksheet within the existing master spreadsheet.
4. Name the worksheet using the event number and event title.
5. Generate the appropriate column headers based on the registration form fields.
6. Save the worksheet ID or tab identifier against the event record in the website database.

For example:

- Event 001 – Online Business Meetup & Spotlight
- Event 002 – Business Growth Masterclass
- Event 003 – Business Finance Workshop
- Event 004 – Founder Roundtable

Use a unique event ID internally to prevent duplicate tabs.

Do not create a new worksheet every time an event is edited or republished.

C. AUTOMATIC REGISTRATION DATA SYNC

Whenever someone submits an event registration form:

1. Validate the submitted information.
2. Save the registration in the website database.
3. Identify the event associated with the registration.
4. Automatically send the registration details to the corresponding event worksheet.
5. Also append the registration to the central ALL REGISTRATIONS worksheet.
6. Update the event registration statistics.

Every registration must be associated with its correct event.

For example, a participant registering for Event 001 must appear in:

- Event 001's dedicated worksheet.
- The ALL REGISTRATIONS worksheet.

A participant registering for Event 002 must appear in:

- Event 002's dedicated worksheet.
- The ALL REGISTRATIONS worksheet.

Never mix event-specific records in the wrong worksheet.

D. REGISTRATION DATA STRUCTURE

Each event worksheet should contain the relevant fields from that event's registration form.

For the inaugural event, include:

- Registration ID
- Registration Date
- Full Name
- Email Address
- Phone / WhatsApp Number
- Country
- City / State
- Occupation / Participant Category
- Business Name
- Business Description
- Industry
- Business Age
- Business Stage
- Website / Social Media Link
- Number of Employees
- Revenue Status
- Monthly Revenue Range
- Business Registration Status
- Financial Record-Keeping Status
- Operational Systems Status
- Biggest Business Challenges
- Business Priorities
- Learning Expectations
- Question for Guest Speaker
- Consulting Interest
- Investable Business Playbook Interest
- Investment-Readiness Interest
- Follow-up Interest
- Marketing Consent
- Communication Preferences
- Attendance Status
- Follow-up Status

Include submission timestamps and event identification fields.

Only collect fields actually included in the relevant event's registration form. If a future event has different questions, its worksheet should reflect those questions.

The ALL REGISTRATIONS worksheet should contain a common set of fields, including Event ID, Event Name, Registration ID, submission date, participant details and relevant business information. Preserve event-specific answers in their dedicated worksheets.

E. OVERVIEW DASHBOARD

Create an overview dashboard inside the master Google Spreadsheet.

The dashboard should automatically display:

- Total number of events.
- Total registrations across all events.
- Total registrations per event.
- Registrations received this month.
- Registrations by industry.
- Registrations by business stage.
- Registrations by location.
- Participants interested in consulting.
- Participants interested in investment-readiness services.
- Attendance statistics, where available.

Use formulas, pivot tables or automatically refreshed summaries.

The dashboard should update whenever new registration records are added.

F. ADMIN DASHBOARD INTEGRATION

Inside the website's admin dashboard, provide a Google Sheets integration settings area.

Display:

- Google Sheets connection status.
- Master spreadsheet name.
- Spreadsheet link.
- Spreadsheet connection status.
- Number of event worksheets created.
- Last successful synchronisation.
- Failed synchronisation count.

Provide administrator controls to:

- Connect Google Sheets.
- Select or configure the master spreadsheet.
- Test the connection.
- Retry failed synchronisations.
- View the associated worksheet for each event.
- Open the master spreadsheet directly.

The administrator should not need to manually create tabs or copy registrations.

G. DATA RELIABILITY AND ERROR HANDLING

The integration must be reliable.

Implement the following:

- Secure Google Sheets API integration.
- Store Google credentials securely on the server, never in frontend code.
- Use unique registration IDs.
- Prevent duplicate rows when a sync is retried.
- Track sync status for each registration.
- Implement automatic retry for temporary Google API failures.
- Log synchronisation errors.
- Provide an admin-visible indication of failed or pending synchronisations.
- Never silently discard a registration if Google Sheets is temporarily unavailable.
- Keep the website database as the primary source of truth.
- Provide a way to reconcile missing spreadsheet entries.

Use a reliable background job or server-side process for synchronisation rather than relying on the visitor's browser to write directly to Google Sheets.

H. DATA PRIVACY AND ACCESS

- Do not make the master spreadsheet publicly accessible.
- Restrict access to authorised AffluentAccelerators team members.
- Never expose Google credentials, API keys or service account secrets.
- Respect participant privacy and consent preferences.
- Do not export private participant data into public event pages.
- Ensure only authorised administrators can access registration records.

I. FUTURE SCALABILITY

This integration must support an unlimited number of future events within the same master spreadsheet, subject to Google Sheets capacity and API limits.

The system should dynamically recognise new events, create their worksheets, map their registration fields and begin collecting registrations without requiring code changes for each new event.

FINAL REQUIREMENT:

One website. One central Google Spreadsheet. Multiple event-specific worksheets. Automatic registration collection and synchronisation.

The objective is to give The AffluentAccelerators a centralised event registration and business intelligence database that grows with every webinar, masterclass, workshop and business event we organise.
